$comment: i76motion v1: the haptics host's own motion datagram (docs/MOTION-OUTPUT.md 3.3). Read by tools/haptics/motion/i76motion.py to decode and asserted against Renderers/Udp.I76Motion.cs by the C# motion tests, so the layout cannot drift. Little-endian, no padding. One datagram per output tick, default UDP port 7677 (7676 is the raw i76tel feed).
name: i76motion

conventions.frame: car body frame. Vectors (right, up, forward).
conventions.translation: surge + forward, sway + right, heave + up; m/s^2; gravity EXCLUDED (a parked car reads 0; slope reaches the rig through pitch / roll)
conventions.rotation: aerospace body convention (right-hand rule about forward / right / down): roll + = right side down, pitch + = nose up, yaw + = nose turning right. heading: 0 = facing I'76 world +z, increasing clockwise seen from above, -pi..pi
conventions.cues: cue_surge / cue_sway / cue_heave carry ONLY event spikes (impact, a_diff impulse, landing, explosion, optional shot recoil); total felt acceleration = physics + cue
conventions.neutral: status bit5 set = the host is ramping (or has ramped) every kinematic channel to 0 (stale telemetry, player absent / destroyed, startup hold); a consumer driving actuators must also treat 500 ms without a packet as an E-stop

status_bits.0: live: player present, physics fresh, not destroyed
status_bits.4: paused: no telemetry frames for stale_ms (host alive)
status_bits.5: fail-to-neutral active (ramping to or held at neutral, or ramping back)
status_bits.6: sample is interpolated between two physics states

fields: motion clock: engine sim time in a replay (plus stalled intervals), host time live
